I'm an anti-vaxxer, I'll wait a couple years, and see if it works as advertised, and see if there are any side-effects. My main problem with vaccines is that some of them have serious side-effects, and the flu vaccine in particular doesn't work most of the time.

Universal should be put in parenthesis. This is a vaccine against 4 serotypes of hemagglutinin, the H in H1N1. There are 18 known hemagglutinins(HA), though not all have been isolated in people. The study claims cross protection for 4 additional HA, but cross protection is already a known factor in current Flu vaccines. The only difference I can see between this vaccine and current ones is it uses HA only, whereas current shots also include neuraminidase, the N in H1N1. Furthermore it only used mouse death as a measure of protection, not whether the disease was contracted or not.

Eisenhower famously said:

"Should any political party attempt to abolish social security, unemployment insurance and eliminate labor laws and farm programs, you would not hear of that party again in our political history. There is a tiny splinter group, of course, that believes that you can do these things. Among them are a few Texas oil millionaires, and an occasional politician or businessman from other areas. Their number is negligible and they are stupid."

But this sentiment wasn't just because he thought the political price of abolishing such programs was too high. He believed they were sound public policy:

"Retirement systems, by which individuals contribute to their own security according to their own respective abilities, have become an essential part of our economic and social life. These systems are but a reflection of the American heritage of sturdy self-reliance which has made our country strong and kept it free; the self-reliance without which we would have had no Pilgrim Fathers, no hardship-defying pioneers, and no eagerness today to push to ever widening horizons in every aspect of our national life.

The Social Security program furnishes, on a national scale, the opportunity for our citizens, through that same self-reliance, to build the foundation for their security. We are resolved to extend that opportunity to millions of our citizens who heretofore have been unable to avail themselves of it."

You can read more of Eisenhower's statements on social programs here.

One mans quest to bury the Wild West mystery of Billy the Kids death

I've always found William McCarty/Antrim/Bonney/Billy the Kid to be historically fascinating. Almost everything we know about him is highly suspect. The people who say he was shot by Garrett are all, IMO, biased sources. Garrett wanted to protect his reputation. Interestingly, many Mexicans in the territory also claimed he was dead. But then, The Kid was very popular with the Mexicans of the area and was hunted by the law. It's not unreasonable to say that these people also had a strong motive for lying- protecting a friend.

His reputation as a "quick draw" gunman has also come under question. Eugene Cunningham points out in his book "A Gallery of Gunfighters" that The Kid tended to shoot people in the back, or when he had an advantage. Cunningham called him an efficient killer, but showing no real "triggernometry", as Cunningham calls pistol skill in his book.

I like to think that The Kid somehow outwitted Garrett and escaped. Realistically though, Garrett probably killed him.
